title: Unbounded knapsack: fewest coins
summary: Fewest coins that make an amount, with unlimited coins of each value, or -1. dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a - coin] + 1), walking amounts upward so a coin can be reused. O(len(coins) × amount).
code: # Walk amounts upward so a coin can be reused within the same pass.
return dp[amount] if dp[amount] != inf else -1
triggers: fewest pieces, or the number of ways, to build a total from reusable parts
an unlimited supply of each item and a target sum
prompts: A vending machine gives change in a few coin values and never runs out of any. What is the smallest number of coins that pays out an exact amount?
Floor tiles come in a handful of lengths, unlimited of each. Cover a corridor of exact length with as few tiles as possible, or report that it can't be done.
invariant: After a coin is processed, dp[a] is the fewest coins that make a using only the coins seen so far, repeats allowed.
mantra: Reuse allowed: walk the amount up, plus one coin.
pitfalls: Seed dp[0] = 0 and every other amount with infinity; amounts never reached stay infinite and become -1.
Walking amounts upward reuses a coin; walking downward allows each coin once (0/1 knapsack).
Counting ways adds instead of taking the minimum, with coins in the outer loop so each combination is counted once.

anchors.name: Coin Change II
anchors.trick: Count ways: dp[a] += dp[a - coin], coins in the outer loop.

anchors.name: Perfect Squares
anchors.trick: The coins are the squares up to n.

anchors.name: Combination Sum IV
anchors.trick: Amounts in the outer loop count ordered sequences instead.

mutations.explanation: Forgets to count the coin just used, so every reachable amount reports 0 coins.
Walking downward allows each coin at most once, so amounts that need a repeated coin look impossible.
